input.quote: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Arizona, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof.
input.rationale: Governing law is Arizona, which is outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales), so the clause fails both the preferred and the fallback position. There is no court venue provision; instead Section 19 sends all disputes to mandatory binding arbitration under U.S. Arbitration & Mediation rules, whereas the playbook requires courts as the dispute forum. The arbitration is administered domestically (no foreign seat) and Arizona is not the counterparty's foreign home forum, so this is a deviation rather than walk-away territory. Redline moves law and exclusive venue to New York County courts per the preferred position, with Delaware, California or England and Wales/London offered as fallback.

proposal.summary: Move governing law from Arizona to New York, add exclusive New York County venue, and replace mandatory arbitration with the same courts.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We moved governing law and venue to our accepted New York position and replaced mandatory arbitration with the exclusive jurisdiction of the New York County courts; Arizona law and administered arbitration are outside our accepted list. Delaware, California or England and Wales with London courts would also work if New York is difficult.

ops.oldText: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Arizona, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof.
ops.newText: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof, and each party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York.

ops.oldText: will be subject to and resolved by binding arbitration pursuant to the Arbitration Rules of U.S. Arbitration & Mediation, (www.usam.com). Any award or order rendered by the arbitrator may be confirmed as a judgment or order in any state or federal court of competent jurisdiction, which includes within the federal judicial district of the residence of the party against whom such award or order was entered.
ops.newText: will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York, and each party irrevocably consents to venue in such courts.
